about: SEGA Rally Championship (1995) handling for SR3's ten cars. Only these numbers ship; the files are built from the owner's own SR3 files by build_flavor.py.

sources.gears_kmh_per_1000rpm: MAME srallyc autopilot + owner laps (ElSemi, Mountain): AT upshifts 80/150/181 km/h at ~8000 rpm, 3rd 22.4-23.0, 4th 26.1-27.1 km/h per 1000 rpm, limiter 8800 (agent_handling\run_*, laps\)
sources.grip: sustained lateral (0.5 s median, p95): tarmac 2.65-2.75 g (owner, Mountain), gravel 2.35 g and dirt 2.41 g (autopilot, Desert): gravel/tarmac 0.87
sources.celica_vs_delta: identical in SRC (frame-identical logs), so one set for all cars

gearbox.slip_note: SRC targets 9.6 / 18.9 / 22.7 / 26.6 divided by what test 2 measured of its design (0.81 / 0.82 / 0.86 / 0.91: SR3 tyres run 10-20 % slip when traction-limited)
gearbox.upshift_note: test 3: 1->2 at 82.9 km/h, 2->3 at 165.9 km/h with 0.91 (2nd runs 20.7 km/h per 1000 rpm at speed); SRC 81 / 150 / 181

steering: SEGA Rally 3's own steering chain for the wheels; the TURNING (yaw rate, side velocity) of a car on these files is SEGA Rally Championship's own, set after every vehicle step by the launcher's SRC port (tools/srcport.c, kb 29 section 12), which recognises these files by their Tyre_Road tyre. Force model back to SR3's PowerslideSteer (2): the port replaces the model's turning, and model 1 (SegaRally) left the cars without turning (owner, 2026-10-15)
